items.title: Amazon's Lord of the Rings Gandalf Costume Has Dropped to Its Lowest Price of the Year
items.content_text: October 31 is nearly here and time is running out to buy yourself a costume. This is the week that Spirit Halloween starts to look fully picked over and popular costumes become incredibly scarce. Thankfully, If you happen to have an Amazon Prime membership, there are a number of options still available that will actually ship to you on time. And if you're a Lord of the Rings fan specifically, this official Gandalf costume is an excellent choice for the price. At $36.33 for the XL size, it's surprisingly affordable for an officially licensed costume. It doesn't come with a fake beard or a wig, but if you already have either of those things then you're set. And if you don't, you should be able to find that still in stock somewhere before Halloween. The costume you are buying here is specifically the robe, hat, and belt that were designed after the iconic wizard from Middle-earth. This is a version of Gandalf the Gray, as seen in The Hobbit movie , rather than the more majestic Gandalf the White we got in the later LOTR movies . Like most affordable costumes, it's made of 100% polyester, which means you probably don't want to toss it into the wash with the rest of your clothes. The main issue with this costume, like I mentioned above, is that it isn't exactly complete. If you want to look like Gandalf and not just some random wizard, you will need a gray beard and a gray wig. You'll also likely want some sort of gnarled staff, which can honestly just be a cool tree branch you find in the forest. Thankfully Amazon also has a perfect wig and beard combo in stock that will arrive before Halloween. When Is the Last Day to Buy a Costume on Amazon? At the time of writing, this costume is eligible for two-day Prime shipping, which means it will arrive three days before the actual holiday. Not everything at Amazon is available that fast, but you can assume that there will always be something available within that two-day window on Amazon. That means the last day to buy a costume online is likely October 29, but that will be cutting it really close.

items.title: Dead by Daylight Devs Explain Chucky's Exit From Stores and Says Horror Icons Removed Due to Licenses Have 'Open Invitation' to Rejoin
items.excerpt: Dead by Daylight developer Behaviour Interactive has responded after confirming Chucky would be removed from stores last week, explaining that horror icons will "continue to have an open invitation to join (or rejoin)."
items.content_text: Dead by Daylight developer Behaviour Interactive has responded after confirming Chucky would be removed from stores last week, explaining that horror icons will "continue to have an open invitation to join (or rejoin)." There was a bit of confusion amongst fans when the studio behind the hit asymmetrical horror game announced Chucky as the latest icon to leave its roster . Following the removal of Pinhead last year and Michael Myers just months ago, fans were sad to see another Killer exit stores so soon. However, it's ultimately not up to Behaviour when it comes to the date some franchises may depart. In a statement sent to IGN, Behaviour said that, while its "goal is always to keep licenses" in Dead by Daylight forever, that can't always be the case. That's why, "despite our best efforts," Chucky and others have left and could continue to leave in the future. No one wants to see Dead by Daylight's staggering roster of Killers and Survivors shrink for any reason, especially when Behaviour has consistently delivered variety in the decade since its launch . Unfortunately, that's what will happen come November 24, 2026, when the Chucky Chapter is made unavailable to purchase. The upside, as Behaviour made clear in last week's announcement, is that anyone who purchases the possessed killer doll and any of his accompanying cosmetics will have the freedom to use them beyond the cutoff date. It means that, while Chucky may show up in fewer lobbies over time, he'll never truly be gone. It's something Behaviour made sure to reiterate in its statement to IGN, reassuring fans that "Dead by Daylight will always be gaming's House of Horror." This means that, even when licenses expire, the Child's Play , Halloween, and Hellraiser franchises will always have the same invitation to enter the Fog that newcomers have. You can see the studio's full statement on Chucky's exit below. "As with all live service games, players can expect regular updates, new content, and occasional changes over time," Behaviour said. "Our goal is always to keep licenses in our game forever. When they have to go away, it's because - despite our best efforts - it wasn't possible to retain them. "We want to reassure our community that Chucky will remain part of the Dead by Daylight experience for existing owners. Players who already own The Good Guy, his perks, or any associated cosmetics will still be able to use that content after November 24, 2026. "Dead by Daylight will always be gaming's House of Horror, and horror icons will continue to have an open invitation to join (or rejoin) us in the Fog." It'll be painful to see one of Dead by Daylight's more unique Killers leave the Fog, but a return is definitely not off the table. One of the more famous examples of an IP leaving and eventually coming back was Stranger Things and its playable Demogorgon, which was removed from stores in November 2021 before being added back in November 2023. For now, there's no telling when Chucky and Child's Play may return. Meanwhile, we recently found out that Terrifier's Art the Clown would enter the fray starting next month. Friday the 13th's Jason was added in June. For more, you can check out everything Behaviour announced during its 10th Anniversary Broadcast over the summer.
items.title_en: Dead by Daylight Devs Explain Chucky's Exit From Stores and Says Horror Icons Removed Due to Licenses Have 'Open Invitation' to Rejoin

items.title: DC Studios Boss Confirms Discussions With Alan Ritchson, But Haven't Found a Role for Him Yet
items.excerpt: DC Studios boss Peter Safran confirms they've had conversations with Alan Ritchson for a variety of roles, but are still looking to find the right one.
items.content_text: DC Studios boss Peter Safran confirms they've had conversations with Alan Ritchson for a variety of roles, but are still looking to find the right one. When speaking with Collider , Safran confirmed that Ritchson is an actor with whom DC Studios has had several conversations and wants to utilize. He noted that they've eyed him for a handful of projects, but none of them have come to fruition. Although the actor has been heavily speculated about and is on fans' wishlist to play the DCU's Batman, it doesn't sound like that's the role DC wants him for . However, DC sees more in him than just a big badass brawler, which is the kind of role he's best known for. "[...] He's just good," said Safran. "I also think there's a lot more depth to him than you might have seen. I think there's more that he can do that people haven't seen." It's unclear what roles he could play. Obviously, given his size, he's a great fit for someone like Bane, Deathstroke, or some other physically imposing character. However, it sounds like Safran is trying to find something that allows him to flex his acting chops and show off his range. DC is currently producing a film centered around Bane and Deathstroke, so it's possible he ends up playing one of those characters, but it's hard to say right now. Although Robert Pattinson is currently firmly seated in the role of Batman, he's not expected to play the character in the DCU. Pattinson himself has even noted that the tonal difference between his DC universe and James Gunn's might be too jarring . Instead, the DCU is expected to introduce an older Batman with a son, Damian Wayne. It's unclear when we will actually see him or when we will learn who is playing him, as the project was announced nearly four years ago and has received very few updates. The DCU's Batman was briefly seen in Creature Commandos, but it wasn't anything super notable. The character does not appear in DC's Clayface movie, either, so the studio is clearly trying to find the right way to properly introduce him. Maybe he'll be in next year's Man of Tomorrow, but we'll just have to wait and see.

items.title: Canceled Transformers Game Footage Leaks Online, Showing Never-Before-Seen Final Trailer
items.excerpt: A final trailer for the canceled game Transformers: Reactivate has leaked online, giving fans the closest look at what the completed project might’ve looked like.
items.content_text: A final trailer for the canceled game, Transformers: Reactivate, has leaked online, giving fans the closest look at what the completed project might’ve looked like. Transformers: Reactivate , a third-person online action game made by developer Splash Damage, was first revealed at the 2022 Game Awards. The title faced major delays after its big reveal and was eventually canned in January 2025, with Splash Damage undergoing several rounds of layoffs in the nearly two years since then. Just a day after the project was put to bed, gameplay footage from the highly-anticipated title leaked online, showing Bumblebee blasting enemies and traversing terrain in his vehicle form. It’s been more than a year since this footage found its way on social media, but in a miraculous turn of events, one fan has managed to uncover a final trailer for the game with what seems to be the most complete build we’ve seen thus far. The trailer was uploaded to X/Twitter on October 26, 2026 by a user named 'Nem - TFR Archives' who, by their own admission, preserves Transformers: Reactive content because they "need to cope somehow." Preceding the footage is a message from Nem, which speculates that the trailer was created as an investment pitch to other publishers that "ultimately failed." What’s more, this trailer shows off what appears to be a fully-fledged campaign, with Nem saying the project shifted from a purely free-to-play online experience to a title with much more single-player content and optional online co-op. The trailer shows Optimus Prime (seemingly not voiced by Peter Cullen, with users speculating he is instead played by Jon Bailey, who has also given voice to several Transformers characters in the past, including Optimus), saying that the Legion has invaded the galaxy and that it’s up to the Autobots to seek them out and prevent further destruction. Footage shows Optimus, Bumblebee, and Iron Hide navigating rough terrain as they fend off the Legion, eventually teaming up with the Decepticons to purge the galaxy of this mutual enemy. It seems Megatron was a recruitable and playable character, who used a whip-like appendage, as well as a gun, to take down his foes. Given what we’ve seen thus far, it’s even more of a travesty that this game was canceled. Transformers fans almost had something amazing on their hands, with an intriguing story, stunningly realistic visuals, and what appeared to be robust gameplay that utilized both Autobots and Decepticons. Here it is the final trailer of transformers reactivate their latest version of the game. as you see totally different from what y'all ever seen. In it you can see: New York, Nevada desert and Cybertron. you can see bits of gameplay there and there and final designs of the cast. https://t.co/qtq0bXHIw7 — 𝓔𝓷𝓭𝓮𝓻🔛🔝 (@EnderGuyZV2) October 26, 2026 Nem is currently making a documentary about this failed project and is urging anyone with information and willing to share their story to reach out to them at a proton email linked in their bio. Transformers: Reactive is far from the only painful cancellation to happen in the gaming space; the next Mass Effect game was also canned by EA, which shut down BioWare as part of its shift in strategy, leaving fans brokenhearted and doing everything they can to get the title out of limbo and into the hands of another developer.

items.title: Want To Smell Like a Werfwulf? This Perfume Has You Covered
items.content_text: Nothing says date night like the smell of "the heat of flesh that was once human." Robert Eggers' Werwulf hits movie theaters at Christmas, but you can pre-order an official perfume set based on the movie right now. Focus Features has teamed up with the very fancy Heretic Parfum for a set of three very specific fragrances. Designed to represent each stage of a werewolf transformation, the descriptions of each of the scents are a wild ride. The Wode Hath Teth: The scent of the feral woodland itself. Cold bark, frozen soil, and smoke in the air. Resinous. Mineral. Austere. Werwulf: The transformation. Skin, damp earth, root, resin, and the suggestion of wet fur. Intimate. Warm. Primal. Blodwode: The memory of what the forest has witnessed. Bleeding tree bark, leather, musk, and the heat of flesh that was once human. Animalic. Resinous. Untamed. The set is limited edition, $55, and won't ship until at least November 6, but at least that's in time for Grandma's Christmas present. You can also grab each perfume individually for $125. It's not the first movie collaboration Heretic has done. Nosferatu Eau de Macabre used notes of "wilting lilacs, velvety vegan ambergris and strikes of lightning" while one for the The Bride promised "Jasmine and rose stitched together as flesh. Cedarwood as bone. Frankincense as breath or spirit." The company is perhaps most notorious for creating the viral “This Smells Like My Vagina” candle with Gwyneth Paltrow in 2020.
items.title_en: Want To Smell Like a Werfwulf? This Perfume Has You Covered

items.title: Hunger Games Director Hopes You Aren't Too Distracted With GTA 6 to See Sunrise on the Reaping
items.excerpt: Francis Lawrence, director of Netflix’s BioShock movie, opened up to IGN about his favorite video games of all time, and we have to admit that he knows ball.
items.content_text: Francis Lawrence, director of Netflix’s BioShock movie, opened up to IGN about his favorite video games of all time, and we have to admit that he knows ball. You might know Lawrence from his work on the Hunger Games films. He's directed almost every single one of them, after all, most recently lending his talents to the upcoming prequel film Sunrise on the Reaping , which hits theaters this November. With a slew of blockbuster adaptations under his belt, Lawrence is now helming the live-action BioShock movie at Netflix — a project that's nearly 20 years in the making. Given he’s a self-professed fan of the series, we had to ask about his favorite games of all time. "Well, the big ones for me were Metal Gear Solid , BioShock, and Call of Duty, " he answered. "I'd say the original GTA . I don't think I played beyond the original GTA, but the original one was pretty wild when that came out, the sort of technology of it. But I think those were all kind of my favorites." When we brought up the imminent release of GTA 6 — arguably the most technologically advanced game in the franchise and one of the most highly anticipated pop culture launches of all time — Lawrence bemoaned how close the game's release is to Sunrise on the Reaping. "Unfortunately, I think it comes out right around the same time our movie does. Hopefully, people find time for both. Play GTA, go see our movie, play more GTA," he joked. We got the chance to chat with Lawrence about his BioShock movie , which he said was initially brought to him by Gore Verbinski back in 2009. However, due to scheduling conflicts, he wasn’t able to take the project. Guillermo del Toro was later in talks to direct the film, but "didn’t see eye-to-eye" with the game’s creator, as Lawrence put it. The version of events that Guillermo del Toro gave to us, however, was far less mild. "We had a very contentious call about a couple of games," he told us as part of our IGN30 Icons interview series. "...So adapting it, BioShock, we had a couple of calls. They are probably one of the most disastrous calls I've ever had. So no, f**k no." Lawrence is also gearing up to direct a film adaptation of Red Rising , a young adult book series written by author Peirce Brown. That project, too, has been in development hell, but finally found a home at Paramount and a writer to pen the script.
items.title_en: Hunger Games Director Hopes You Aren't Too Distracted With GTA 6 to See Sunrise on the Reaping

items.title: Red Rising Director Francis Lawrence Says YA Series' Movie Adaptation Is a 'Priority' at Paramount Following Shelved Netflix Show
items.excerpt: We got the chance to chat with Francis Lawrence, director of the forthcoming Red Rising movie, who let us in on some exciting updates about the project and its current status at Paramount.
items.content_text: We got the chance to chat with Francis Lawrence, director of the forthcoming Red Rising movie, who let us in on some exciting updates about the project and its current status at Paramount. Francis Lawrence might as well be the end-all, be-all of young adult book-to-screen adaptations. Best known for directing almost every single movie in the Hunger Games series, Lawrence recently helmed The Long Walk and is following that up with the next Hunger Games movie, Sunrise on the Reaping , in November. Given his extensive pedigree with YA literature adaptations, we had to quiz him about the upcoming Red Rising movie , the long-awaited adaptation of author Pierce Brown’s galaxy-spanning sci-fi epic. According to Lawrence, multiple "regime changes" at Netflix — where the movie was first set to release — set things back, but after eight long years, it finally found a home at Paramount. "I have been attached to Red Rising for about eight years, and Pierce [Brown] and I have become friends. The books were actually brought to me by my producing partner, Cam [MacConomy], who's a producer on this movie and has worked with me since 2010. He found the books and brought [them] to me, and I fell in love with them, and Cam is in love with them. We met with Pierce and we brought it out to market and went to Netflix. We were going to do it as a series, originally. Unfortunately, our experience at Netflix — we had two amazing pilots written, but regimes kept changing and they kept creating these departments of 'tentpole, now it's YA, back to tentpole again,'" he explained. "It was getting bounced around, and it's not a cheap [project] to make and to do it right. They never got the guts to pull the trigger on it. And so, the rights reverted back to Pierce. Pierce then went to Paramount, which I was happy about, because I actually prefer the theatrical approach for Red Rising rather than streaming, because I think it's a series that's definitely deserving of a theatrical experience and IMAX and the whole thing. "I'm very, very excited about that. We have a writer that we like, who is now starting work on a script, and hopefully that's something that we will put together quite quickly. It seems to be a priority at Paramount, which is great. Super, super, super excited about that. But I love the books and I love Pierce and I'm really, really excited." Despite the news going public just two weeks ago, Lawrence has been eagerly involved in this project for almost a decade, and it — much like the highly-anticipated BioShock movie — is finally moving forward after years of red tape and production complications. Speaking of BioShock, Lawrence opened up about the forthcoming film and gave us all the gritty details as to why it’s taken so long to get made, but assured us that, as a gamer, he’s doing everything he can to be as faithful to the source material as possible. items.title: GTA 6 Causes 17% Spike in Time Off Requests on Game's Release Date
items.excerpt: GTA 6's release has led to as much as a 17% increase in time-off requests, according to a new report.
items.content_text: GTA 6's release has led to as much as a 17% increase in time-off requests, according to a new report. As reported by Money.com , new data from HR software company BambooHR revealed that there has been a notable spike in time-off requests for November 19. BambooHR revealed that there has been an increase between 9% to 17% on November 19, compared to normal requests for the third Thursday in November. While we aren't sure if every single person is taking that day off to play GTA 6, it stands to reason that this is what the bulk of these requests are for. Economists have estimated a $1 billion loss in productivity in the United States due to GTA 6's release. While we'll just have to wait and see what kind of impact the game has on the world, it is clear that this is a massive event. There's a high level of anticipation for GTA 6, and it is expected to have one of the biggest entertainment launches of all time, if not the biggest. Rockstar has also been spending a ton of money to get the word out with extravagant marketing; it spent $975,000 to install a massive neon pink sign on top of the Miami Heat's arena, after all. The developer also covered the city with in-universe ads for brands in the game, along with more traditional banners featuring the game's key art. Fans can even eat at a real life version of Burger Shot , a fast food chain in the GTA universe, if they live in Miami. There will also be an unprecedented NBA game between the Miami Heat and the Milwaukee Bucks on November 18, which will turn the Heat into the Vice City Heat . They will play with GTA 6-themed jerseys on a never-before-seen Vice City court. It should be quite the spectacle, and serve as an effective final marketing beat for the game. GTA 6 will release on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. A PC port is also rumored for early 2027.

items.title: Composer Austin Wintory Shares 22 Minutes of Music Created for BioWare's Canceled Mass Effect 5
items.excerpt: Composer Austin Wintory was once in talks to make music for Mass Effect 5, and now that EA has shuttered BioWare and canceled the game, he's released his drafts online.
items.content_text: Composer Austin Wintory was once in talks to make music for Mass Effect 5. Now that EA has shuttered BioWare and canceled the game , he's released his drafts online. The award-winning composer behind Sword of the Sea, Journey, and a laundry list of other video games, movies, and shows revealed that he had been in talks to create music for the now-canceled Mass Effect revival in a post on social media. Whether he would have gone on to officially create music for what was in development under the name Mass Effect: Universe is unclear, but judging by the 22 minutes of audio published online for fans, it's clear there was some weight behind those early talks. Wintory called Mass Effect an "all-time dream project" that never came to be. Any hope to continue working on the series seems to have been dashed, which is why any drafts he managed to drum up can now be found on YouTube . It's yet another sneak peek at a project that will likely never see the light of day, and unfortunately for the millions of Mass Effect fans still out there, it's quite good. So here you go ... Thank you again to my friends at both BioWare and EA. To even dream in your sandbox was a privilege https://t.co/wmq2N7s6Kp — Austin Wintory (@awintory) October 26, 2026 "Working on Mass Effect 5 was my career's biggest dream project, my white whale," he said in the description of his YouTube upload. "It is my favorite franchise of all time, and for the last couple years I'd been in serious conversations with BioWare and EA to jump in. My suggestion was to treat the original game's masterful Jack Wall / Sam Hulick score as a starting point, and to build on it from there with deeper use of physical, analog synths, and a more tightly interwoven use of the orchestra. But a love letter first and foremost (not unlike my approach to the Aliens franchise with Fireteam Elite)." Wintory explained that it was during these talks his excitement led him to surprise EA and BioWare with an "elaborate production" consisting of 20 minutes of music for whatever the next Mass Effect would become. Its plot details were a mystery at the time, with the composer clarifying that the music we hear today is "just pure musical exploration." Still, his past as a Mass Effect fan, which dates all the way back to the release of the original game in 2007, is pretty easy to feel. Wintory added that it was "fully recorded and produced with synths, vocals, and a large orchestra" in Los Angeles. It may have been reworked, rearranged, or maybe even scrapped altogether by the time an official release rolled around, but that didn't stop the composer from putting his heart into it. "Receiving the news alongside everyone else that EA had decided to not only cancel the project but shutdown BioWare entirely was a deeply felt loss," he added. "It's been hard to see dear friends lose their jobs, and this beloved franchise seemingly vanish forever." In follow-up posts on social media, Wintory said he hopes his drafts do justice to the work of Wall and Hulick, calling his unofficial entry in the Mass Effect universe a "pure love letter." He added, "So here you go ... Thank you again to my friends at both BioWare and EA. To even dream in your sandbox was a privilege." BioWare's demise has rocked the games industry . After decades of delivering some of the most groundbreaking stories gaming has ever seen, EA announced it would be closing the studio and canceling its Mass Effect 5 last week. Even if it's bittersweet, leaked materials have emerged in the wake of the studio's closure, giving everyone a peek behind the curtain not only at what could have been but just how far along development managed to get . With a trailer for Mass Effect: Universe online and plenty of gameplay details there for fans to pour through, the franchise's community of sci-fi enjoyers has done what they can to fight for a revival. A petition garnering more than 230,000 signatures and a Times Square billboard are just the tip of the iceberg , and even if nothing tangible comes of it, their dedication remains as a testament to the impact BioWare and the developers it's housed over the years have had on millions. For more, you can see how BioWare left a mark not only on players but other game developers , too. You can also read an opinion piece from IGN's Matt Purslow, which explained why EA never knew what it had with BioWare .
items.title_en: Composer Austin Wintory Shares 22 Minutes of Music Created for BioWare's Canceled Mass Effect 5

items.title: Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced Final Major Content Update Coming This Week
items.excerpt: Ubisoft has detailed Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced's final major content update, revealing a closer look at new game+, Nightmare difficulty, and more.
items.content_text: Ubisoft has detailed Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced 's final major content update, revealing a closer look at new game+, Nightmare difficulty, and more. The publisher behind the Assassin's Creed 4 remake broke down some of the most-requested features finally set to make their way to players in a video published today. It's one last push that's set to drop tomorrow, October 27, to keep players plundering before Edward Kenway sails off into the sunset yet again. New game+ and Nightmare difficulty are no doubt the highlights here. The first addition is mostly self-explanatory, allowing players to start a new save file with all of the tools they gathered from a previous, completed playthrough. It supports up to new game+ 5 and, as detailed by game director Richard Knight, gives players "plenty of opportunities to push your skills to the limit and unlock exclusive rewards." If running it back through the West Indies isn't enough of a challenge, there's Nightmare difficulty. A description for the harder mode's version of Activities, for example, says that "harpooning preys are the most vicious" and "underwater breath is very limited." In addition to making Edward's journey more dangerous, the final major content update is "more spectacular" thanks to a collection of new takedown animations. "And that's not all," Knight said. "Alongside these new features, we've also added new Easter Eggs, a host of rewards to discover – including community-inspired trinkets – new outfits, sails, and even adorable new pet cat skins. "Thank you for your support, fan art, videos, and millions of photos shared in photo mode. It was a real honor to bring back Edward's legacy to life and to see that same excitement find its echo amongst you throughout the year." Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced launched for PC, PlayStation 5, and Xbox Series X/S July 9, 2026. IGN gave it a 9/10 review , saying, "More than just a shinier version of the same game you remember, Assassin’s Creed Black Flag Resynced brings what was already one of the best games in the series up to today’s standards." Title update 1.0.8 will indeed be the final major content update when it launches tomorrow, but Ubisoft may continue to deliver smaller quality-of-life fixes should the opportunity arise. Until then, you can see what percentage of players have struggled to take down those infamous Legendary Ships .

items.title: Calcifer's Yule Log Is Coming Back to HBO Max for the Holiday Season
items.content_text: As streaming services gear up for the holiday season, HBO Max has announced a particularly exciting addition for Studio Ghibli fans: the return of Calcifer's Yule Log. A Warner Bros. press release confirms the ambient video will be making its return to streaming on November 1. While Calcifer's Yule Log first debuted in HBO Max during the 2021 holiday season, it was later removed from the service and largely scraped from the internet. It returns briefly during the holiday season each year as part of HBO Max's "Yule Log" lineup, which has grown to include properties like A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms, Harry Potter, and even Rick and Morty. Warner Bros. has yet to confirm whether the video will remain on the service permanently, or will once again be removed after the holiday season. Howl’s Moving Castle was first published as a book by one of the most influential fantasy authors , Diana Wynne Jones. The Studio Ghibli adaptation, directed by Hayao Miyazaki, was released in theaters in 2004. It’s since grown into one of the animation studio's most popular properties, serving as the basis for tons of merchandise and entire sections of the Ghibli Park . We consider it one of the best Studio Ghibli movies of all time. Calcifer, who was voiced by Tatsuya Gashuin in the original release and Billy Crystal in the English dub, quickly became one of the most popular characters in the animated adaptation. The flaming creature quite literally powers Howl’s titular moving castle, and despite his sassy remarks, offers a surprising amount of warmth in his relationships with Howl and Sophie. While the Yule Log video doesn’t quite focus on the spirit’s boisterous personality, it’s a pleasant holiday offering for Studio Ghibli fans. The 30-minute video, inspired by the "virtual fireplace" trend, shows Calcifer peacefully keeping Howl's fireplace lit alongside music and ambient noises from the film. HBO Max has long been the U.S. streaming home for Studio Ghibli movies , including Howl's Moving Castle. However, plenty of eyes are on the service as Paramount finalizes its acquisition of Warner Bros under the Skydance banner . Some reports are already suggesting that the deal will lead to the merging of the Paramount+ and HBO Max streaming services. Potentially in anticipation of some streaming shake-ups, Shout! Factory has been reprinting its line of Studio Ghibli steelbooks . Howl’s Moving Castle was one of the reprints in the bunch, now available from Amazon for $27.99.

items.title: BioShock Movie Director Francis Lawrence Explains Why It's Taken Hollywood So Long to Adapt the Game
items.excerpt: We got the chance to sit down with Francis Lawrence, the director of Netflix’s in-development BioShock movie, who gave us some of the gritty details as to why this adaptation has taken so long to make.
items.content_text: We got the chance to sit down with Francis Lawrence, the director of Netflix’s BioShock movie, who gave us some of the gritty details as to why this adaptation has taken so long to make. The BioShock movie is a project that’s been floating in limbo for more than a decade. The film initially had Gore Verbinski (Pirates of the Caribbean) attached to direct, but it fell through. Later, Guillermo del Toro was in talks to helm the steampunk movie, but that didn’t work out, either. Now, Lawrence — who directed almost every Hunger Games movie and, most recently, The Long Walk — is taking over. Lawrence chatted about his history with the BioShock movie in an interview for The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping , which comes to theaters next month. When asked about what projects he’d like to adapt in the future, he mentioned BioShock but admitted it’s been “tricky” to translate to the silver screen. “I'm also working on BioShock. That's another one that I've been really trying to get going, which is also at Netflix, which is partially tricky. That's a tricky adaptation, because it's an amazing, amazing world. But as a player, you are the lead character of that story. So cracking that is a tough one, but we're getting close, which is also exciting,” he told us. Lawrence admitted the film has been in his orbit since 2009, saying that Verbinski actually approached him about it — essentially offering it up to him on a silver platter — after his vision for the movie was shot down by Universal. “This thing has kind of been on my radar for a long time, as was The Long Walk," he continued. "The Long Walk was something that I tried to do probably 20 years ago, and then somebody else got the rights, and then it kind of bounced around, bounced around, bounced around, and I sort of tracked it, and then it finally landed in my lap, and I went and made it. I remember BioShock was around 2009, I think Gore Verbinski was going to do it at Universal. But it was a $200 million movie, and he wanted a very specific person in it that was not a star, and it was R-rated. Universal was like, ‘No way are we doing this.’ So Gore actually approached me and asked if I wanted to do it, but I was already doing something else and couldn't. “So since probably 2009, it's kind of been in my orbit and something that's always been percolating a little bit like Long Walk. And then yeah, when Guillermo didn't see eye to eye with some of the — I think it was the creator of the game — and that kind of fell apart, then it came my direction. And so I sort of jumped at the opportunity and so I have been trying to develop that one.” Lawrence’s remark about del Toro not seeing “eye to eye” with BioShock’s creator is a gentle way of putting their conversation; speaking with IGN earlier this year, del Toro told us that he never wants to try his hand at adapting a video game ever again, citing a “disastrous” phone call he had with the folks behind BioShock as the reason why. “We had a very contentious call about a couple of games,” he recalled. “...So adapting it, BioShock, we had a couple of calls. They are probably one of the most disastrous calls I've ever had. So no, f**k no.” Lawrence assured us that he's dedicated to making the movie the best it can be, telling us that he's focused on honoring the source material and making sure the game is faithfully brought to the screen as best it can be. "The creator of BioShock had to basically just give the sign off on me, my knowledge," he said. "Again, [he] wanted to know that I was in love with the spirit of the game. I think he wanted to really protect certain elements and ideas and themes, as one should if you're the creator." You can read more from our interview with Guillermo del Toro , and check out more news about Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping.
